extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants and sponsoring advisors for the Jane Coffin Childs postdoctoral fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program rules for applying to and holding a Jane Coffin Childs postdoctoral fellowship, including eligibility, allowable costs, advisor rules, reporting, and required attendance. Targets applicants and their sponsoring advisors/labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application period and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The online application process opens October 1, 2026 for grants due February 1, 2027 at 3:00pm EST, when the application period closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted via the online application portal before the stated deadline and time (3:00pm EST on Feb 1, 2027).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: No indirect costs are paid to the sponsoring institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and sponsors should plan budgets without expecting institutional overhead or indirect cost reimbursement from the Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be notified by email in mid-May, whether their application has been awarded or declined for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect an email decision in mid-May; the Fund does not provide earlier informal indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research allowance — travel restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The $2000 research allowance should not be used for travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel must be supported by separate travel funds (see next item); do not budget travel expenses from the $2000 research allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel funds
rubrics_metrics.description: There are separate funds ($1800) that are awarded to the Fellow to support travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the designated $1800 travel allocation for travel-related expenses; travel should not be charged to the research allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research allowance — health insurance permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, as long as the sponsor and fellow agree, the research allowance may be used for health insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $2000 research allowance may cover health insurance costs if both sponsor and fellow concur in its use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign national eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, if they are working in a US lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-U.S. citizens are eligible for the fellowship provided their research is conducted in a U.S. laboratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. citizens working abroad
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. citizens conducting postdoctoral work in foreign labs are eligible for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No application feedback provided
rubrics_metrics.description: No, the fund will not provide feedback on applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect critique, reviews, or individualized feedback from the Fund after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisors/co-advisors allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can have one primary postdoctoral advisor and one co-advisor. A co-advisor is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan mentorship accordingly: you may name one primary advisor and optionally one co-advisor in the application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisors cannot serve as referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral advisors and co-advisors CANNOT be referee writers for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee letters must come from individuals other than the primary advisor or co-advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications from same sponsoring lab
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that multiple applications are submitted from the same sponsoring lab, it is the policy of the Fund to award no more than one fellow per sponsor in any award year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labs may submit multiple applications, but at most one award will be made per sponsor in a given award year — consider internal coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor Biosketch and Other Support format
rubrics_metrics.description: We acknowledge that the NIH formats for these documents has been recently updated. You may choose to provide the forms in whichever format you prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may submit advisor biosketch and Other Support documents in either the current NIH format or an earlier format; the Fund has no strict format requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Fellows in a lab
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be TWO Fellows funded by Jane Coffin Childs at any one time over the multi-year award, as long as they are funded in different award years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At most two JCC-funded fellows may be in the same lab simultaneously, provided their award years are different (i.e., staggered funding years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at annual symposium
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, fellows are expected to attend annual symposium for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance at the annual symposium is required for the three-year fellowship period; all meeting expenses for attendees’ travel, lodging, and meals hosted by JCC are paid by JCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fiscal and narrative reports (years 2 and 3 funding dependency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes, funding in years 2 and 3 of the fellowship is dependent on the submission of annual fiscal and narrative reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To receive continuation funding for years 2 and 3, fellows must submit the required annual fiscal and narrative reports on time and in the format requested by the Fund.
